sections.html:
Three routes are open to an Exeter owner: an agent, a sale by owner, or a cash buyer who purchases as-is. The township borders Reading in Berks County. A cash offer makes the most sense if the house needs repairs or you have a deadline.

Exeter is a second class township with 25,466 residents at the 2020 Census and an estimated 26,069 in July 2025. Only Reading and Spring Township are bigger in Berks County. Owner-occupied homes make up 87.1 percent of the total, so few houses are rentals. The typical owned home is valued at $281,800 and median household income is $100,083. About 93.6 percent of residents had not moved in the past year. Monthly cost is typically $1,919 with a mortgage, and rent is typically $1,632.

Names such as Reiffton, Jacksonwald, Stonersville, Lorane, Neversink, Limekiln, Baumstown and Stonetown show up in addresses, yet none is its own municipality. The township issues your zoning and your permits.

Read the zoning code, the historic resource rules and the short-term lodging provisions before you sign anything. The code is online. The Building, Zoning and Engineering department posts forms for building, plumbing, zoning and sign permits, along with a complaint form and a flood plains map.

  • Historic resources: the zoning code sorts historic properties into Classes I to IV and routes changes to them through the Planning Commission and the Board of Supervisors. Class I status requires the owner's written consent and binds heirs and later owners. After a historic resource is demolished through neglect, the township may withhold building and occupancy permits for a year.
  • Short-term lodging: a license from the Zoning Officer lets a property serve as short-term lodging, capped at 90 days per calendar year. Anyone who wants nightly rentals must apply.
  • Floodplain: the township document center holds a flood plains map. Look up your parcel on it.

Tell buyers early if the house is a listed historic resource or lies in a mapped flood area. The Exeter Friends Meeting House, the Mordecai Lincoln House, Boonecroft, Levan Farm, Mill Tract Farm, Snyder Mill and the John Bishop House are on the National Register, and the Daniel Boone Homestead is in the township, so a house nearby may prompt questions.

Berks County last reassessed countywide for the 1994 tax year, which means assessments may be far from today's sale prices. Assessment records are kept at 400 E. Wyomissing Avenue in Mohnton, though that office neither bills nor collects. Your municipal tax collector knows what you owe.

A reduction requires proof that the assessment exceeds current market value, because the law presumes it correct. High taxes or trouble paying do not count. School districts and municipalities can appeal too, often to raise a value.

No age-based or special form freezes or removes property taxes for seniors. Homestead and farmstead exclusions do exist, and the school district supplies the forms.

sections.h2: Recording a deed in Berks County
sections.html:
Recording a document that conveys real estate in Berks County starts at $88. The Recorder of Deeds is on the third floor of the Berks County Services Center, 633 Court Street, Reading. Personal checks are not accepted for transfer tax, and a Statement of Value counts as one extra page when fees are added up.

The state's rate is 1 percent of value, and both parties on the deed are liable. The recorder forwards the state portion to the Department of Revenue and passes any local portion to the municipality or school district. Some family transfers and property that passes by will or intestacy are exempt. For the total at your sale price, phone the Recorder of Deeds.

Homestead and farmstead exclusions exist in Berks County, and the school district supplies the forms. If you claimed one, tell your buyer that a new owner must apply for their own. The Assessment Office holds the records but does not send a bill, so for what you owe, call the municipal tax collector. Ask for the balance in writing so the title company can pay it at settlement.

An annual appeal is a long shot for most sellers, because the law presumes the assessment is correct and you carry the burden of proof. If you already filed and the house sells, tell the buyer, since the result affects the bill they inherit.

Section 7308 of 68 Pa.C.S. does not oblige a seller to inspect the property. It does bar the seller from stating something known to be false or omitting a known material defect. Section 7306 lets a seller answer items outside their knowledge using the best information at hand. The form may be handed over, mailed first class or certified, or faxed, and cash buyers receive it just like everyone else.

Owners choose cash to avoid showings, repair lists and a long wait. In Exeter that might be an estate house to clear out, a home held for decades with deferred upkeep, a move to be near family, or trouble with a short-term lodging license. Compare the offer with what a listing would leave you once repairs and transfer tax are paid, then decide.

sections.h2: Preparing the house and the paperwork
sections.html:
Before a buyer's agent or an investor walks through, walk through yourself. Note anything a disclosure form would ask about, such as past water in the basement, roof leaks, the age of the heating system or work done without a permit. Answer from what you actually know and say so when you do not know.

Collect the deed, recent tax bills, permits, warranty papers and any lease. Look up your parcel on the township's flood plains map. If the house is near one of the listed historic sites, ask the Building, Zoning and Engineering department whether any historic resource rule touches your lot. These small steps keep a deal from stalling after you have already agreed on a price.

Once an offer is accepted, the title company researches the deed history and looks for unpaid taxes or liens. Get any balance from the municipal tax collector, and ask your lender for a payoff if a mortgage is open. Cash buyers have no lender timetable, so the closing date turns on title work and your move.

At closing you sign the deed and settlement papers, and the deed goes to the Berks County Recorder of Deeds. For a rental, bring the lease. For a house that belonged to a relative who has died, bring the papers showing who may sign for the estate.

Complete the seller disclosure carefully and keep permits and repair receipts. Buyers who see full paperwork ask fewer questions, which shortens the path to closing. If you need a few extra days to move out, ask for them in the agreement before you sign.

faqs.q: What decides the closing date on an Exeter Township cash sale?
faqs.a: Title work and the date you prefer, because no lender sets a schedule. The deed is then recorded with the Berks County Recorder of Deeds.

faqs.q: Is Exeter Township part of Reading?
faqs.a: No. Exeter Township is its own municipality in Berks County and borders St. Lawrence borough and Birdsboro. Check your tax bill, since the township, not the city, sets your zoning.

faqs.q: Can I contest my Exeter assessment while the house is listed?
faqs.a: Yes, in the June 15 to August 1 annual window or within 40 days of a change notice. The proof must show the assessment is above market value.

faqs.q: What school district covers Exeter Township?
faqs.a: Exeter Township School District, which also takes in the borough of St. Lawrence. Its buildings are Lorane, Owatin Creek and Jacksonwald elementary schools, Reiffton Elementary School, Exeter Junior High and Exeter Township Senior High.

faqs.q: Can an Exeter house be used for short-term rentals?
faqs.a: Only with a short-term lodging license from the Zoning Officer, and use is capped at 90 days a year. Buyers should check the license first if they count on rental income.
